title: Uniformly bounded affine-line polynomials give finite-coordinate polynomials
statement: Let $K$ be an infinite field [def-weil-field], $W$ a $K$-vector space, $D\geq0$ an integer, and $F:W\to K$ a function. Suppose for every $v,w\in W$ there is $q_{v,w}\in K[T]$ of degree at most $D$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] with $F(tv+w)=q_{v,w}(t)$ for every $t\in K$. Then for every $r\geq0$ and every $e_1,\ldots,e_r\in W$ there is $P\in K[X_1,\ldots,X_r]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] of total degree at most $D$ with $F(\sum_i x_i e_i)=P(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ for every $(x_i)\in K^r$. A polynomial over an infinite field is determined by its values on $K^r$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 10.12 proof, printed p.47, with the uniform degree bound supplied by Proposition 10.13; bounded version and total-degree argument

proof.text: Choose pairwise distinct $c_0,\ldots,c_D\in K$: at each of the $D+1$ choices only finitely many field elements have been excluded, whereas $K$ is infinite. We prove by induction on $n\geq0$, simultaneously for every $w\in W$ and every tuple $e_1,\ldots,e_n$, that $G_{n,w}(x)=F(w+\sum_{i=1}^n x_i e_i)$ is represented by a polynomial of degree at most $D$ in each separate variable. For $n=0$, use the constant polynomial $F(w)$; the ring in no variables is $K$ by its finite-monomial description [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring].

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 10.12 proof, printed p.47, using the uniform degree bound; agent expansion of total-degree and determination arguments.

proof.text: Assume the induction claim for $n-1$. For each $j=0,\ldots,D$, apply it at the translate $w+c_je_n$ to get $P_j\in K[X_1,\ldots,X_{n-1}]$. Put $P=\sum_j P_j L_j(X_n)$ with $L_j$ from [lem-sfb-lagrange-reconstruction]. For a fixed $x\in K^{n-1}$, the hypothesis supplies a polynomial $q_x(T)$ of degree at most $D$ representing $F(Te_n+w+\sum_{i<n}x_ie_i)$. Its values at $c_j$ are $P_j(x)$. Reconstruction therefore gives $P(x,t)=\sum_j P_j(x)L_j(t)=q_x(t)$ for all $t\in K$. Each $L_j$ is a product of $D$ linear factors, so expanding this displayed sum shows that each variable of $P$ has exponent at most $D$: for the first $n-1$ variables this follows from each $P_j$, and for the last from each $L_j$. Polynomial substitution and this coefficient expansion are the operations of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. This proves the induction claim, including repeated or zero $e_i$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 10.12 proof, printed p.47, using the uniform degree bound; agent expansion of total-degree and determination arguments.

proof.text: Polynomial determination follows by induction on $r$. Subtract two polynomials with the same values to obtain $R$ vanishing on $K^r$. For $r=0$, its single value is its constant coefficient. For $r\geq1$, collect monomials as $R=\sum_{i=0}^m A_i(X_1,\ldots,X_{r-1})X_r^i$, using [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. At each $x\in K^{r-1}$ the univariate polynomial $\sum_i A_i(x)T^i$ vanishes at every $t\in K$; [lem-trf-polynomial-infinite-evaluation-identity], with $q=0$, says this polynomial is zero. Thus every $A_i(x)=0$; induction gives $A_i=0$ and hence $R=0$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 10.12 proof, printed p.47, using the uniform degree bound; agent expansion of total-degree and determination arguments.

proof.text:
Apply step 2 with $w=0,n=r$ to obtain a representing polynomial $P$. If $r=0$ or $P=0$, it has total degree at most $D$ (the zero polynomial is allowed). Otherwise write $P=\sum_\alpha a_\alpha X^\alpha$ and let $m$ be the maximum $|\alpha|=\sum_i\alpha_i$ with $a_\alpha
e0$. If $m>D$, the polynomial $H=\sum_{|\alpha|=m}a_\alpha X^\alpha$ is nonzero and homogeneous of degree $m$. By [lem-trf-infinite-field-top-form-direction] choose $v\in K^r$ with $H(v)
e0$. Direct monomial substitution gives $P(Tv)=\sum_\alpha a_\alpha v^\alpha T^{|\alpha|}$, whose coefficient of $T^m$ is $H(v)
e0$ and with no terms above $m$. Thus it has degree $m$. But its values are $F(tu)$ for $u=\sum_i v_i e_i$, which the original hypothesis with $w=0$ represents by $q_{u,0}$ of degree at most $D$. The two univariate polynomials agree at every point of the infinite field, so [lem-trf-polynomial-infinite-evaluation-identity] makes them equal, contradicting $m>D$. Therefore $P$ has total degree at most $D$, completing both conclusions.
